chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I said to him: 'What about those who keep aloof from the great sins and the immoralities except for the 'Lamam'?' He said: 'The defiance after the defiance, i.e., the sin after the sin committed by the servant.'
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Lamam' mean in Quran 53:32 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies that 'Al-Lamam' refers not to minor sins, but to the persistence in sinning after repentance, described as 'defiance after defiance.' This interpretation highlights the spiritual danger of returning to sin, distinguishing it from occasional lapses, and underscores the importance of sincere, lasting repentance in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws), said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘(What about) [53:32] Those who keep aloof from the great sins and the immoralities except for the ‘Lamam’?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The defiance after the defiance i.e., the sin after the sin committed by the man’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once I read the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, before one of the two Imam (a.s.) . . those who avoid the major sins and indecent acts except the al-Lamam ones . . [53:33]
The Imam said, ‘It is a thing after a thing, that is, a sin after a sin that a servant (of Allah) commits.’”
